text:
jordan: hi team, onboarding day 1 on a Windows laptop using WSL2 (Ubuntu). followed the dotfiles and asdf install but rust cargo bins (like cargo-watch) aren't on PATH in VSCode remote terminal. in plain WSL shell `~/.asdf/shims` shows the binaries. any WSL quirks?

tal: welcome! WSL + VSCode Remote can have different shell startup behavior. check if your remote is launching a login shell and whether your dotfiles create symlinks into /usr/local/bin vs ~/bin. also `echo $PATH` inside the VSCode remote terminal vs plain wsl shows differences.

jordan: i see `~/.asdf/shims` in PATH in my tty, but VSCode remote shows PATH missing that entry. my dotfiles symlink `~/bin` -> `.dotfiles/bin` and i put `export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"` in ~/.profile. maybe profile not sourced?

mei: on Ubuntu shells, ~/.profile is read by login shells but not by non-login interactive shells. For WSL, VSCode remote typically uses the login shell? There's also `~/.bashrc` for interactive shells. simplest is to put minimal PATH exports in ~/.profile and source ~/.profile from ~/.bashrc: `if [ -f "$HOME/.profile" ]; then . "$HOME/.profile"; fi`. that makes both interactive and login shells consistent.

jordan: ok i'll try sourcing profile from bashrc. unrelated: when i `cargo install cargo-watch` it puts bin in ~/.cargo/bin but that dir isn't in PATH even after fixing profile. weird.

tal: add `export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"` to your profile. some people add it via `rustup` step but dotfiles may have omitted it. run `source ~/.profile` and `which cargo-watch`.

jordan: did that, now `which cargo-watch` finds it in WSL shell but VSCode remote still can't run it from tasks. tasks.json spawns `/bin/bash -lc` — maybe tasks inherit a fresh non-interactive environment. any workaround?

mei: for tasks, you can set `terminal.integrated.shellArgs.linux` to `['-l']` to force login shell in remote server, or add `"env": { "PATH": "${env:PATH}:$HOME/.cargo/bin" }` in the specific task temporarily. For long term we prefer making login and non-login shells load the same minimal env.

jordan: thanks. another gotcha: asdf python plugin installed but pipx-installed CLIs (like pre-commit) end up in /home/jordan/.local/bin and sometimes Windows-side editors won't pick them up since VSCode Windows client doesn't pass the WSL PATH to the UI. any recommended pattern?

tal: we try to keep editor integrations using the Remote extension (so the server side runs them). For tools that also need Windows-side actions (like native git hooks), prefer installing formatters/linters in CI and using the editor plugin to call remote versions. Also add `~/.local/bin` to PATH in your profile.

jordan: last small question: dotfiles include a `link-dotfiles.sh` that uses `ln -s` and fails when the target exists as a directory. should i `rm -rf` then link or use `stow`?

mei: don't `rm -rf` blindly. we usually use GNU stow or a small script that backs up existing files (mv to filename.pre-onboard) before linking. put backups in `~/dotfiles-backups` and open a PR to our dotfiles repo if you find fragility.

infra-bot: Welcome @jordan! Quick checklist: 1) Add your SSH key to Gitlab 2) Join #dev-setup and #wsl-help 3) Run the onboarding script: https://internal.redwood.dev/onboard 4) If you need access to secure runners, request via #infra-requests.

jordan: awesome, that gives me a path forward. i'll fix the profile/bashrc sourcing, add ~/.cargo/bin and ~/.local/bin to PATH, and switch the dotfiles linker to backup mode before replacing. thanks everyone :raised_hands:
